Medium-term regime (0.20): 25-session block 7132.7 (30 Apr) to 7624.6 (2 Jun) with the close at the 87.9th percentile of the range, still Trending Bullish = +1 -> +0.20; this is the same TREND_UP label that governs Trade 2 on this date and it is reused unchanged. VOLator (0.10): the report's slope is mildly positive but the expansion on 3 June accompanies a down impulse (widest full-day range of the window, 85.4 pts), so expansion-down = -0.5 -> -0.05. Kaufman (0.15): report KER +0.31 x sign of the medium-term move (+) -> +0.047. Sentiment tilt (0.15): report section 13b +0.40 -> +0.060. Cross-asset (0.15): report section 10 MIXED = sign x 0.3 -> +0.045. Total = +0.052, below the 0.25 conviction threshold, so direction = NEUTRAL and Trade 1 is suppressed. The outcome is robust to every free reading in the vector: taking the VOLator term at its most bullish (+0.5 -> +0.05) gives +0.152 and at zero gives +0.102, both NEUTRAL; only flipping the short-term term off Bearish would clear the threshold, and that term is fixed by the 3 June open, close and RSI2 arithmetic. Corroborating the bearish short-term read, the report's own section 16 states that a close below 7566.65 'would neutralise the bullish structure and shift the read to range/transition'; the 3 June cash close of 7565.20 is 1.45 pts below that level, so the report's own invalidation was met on the session it did not see. SUPPRESSION (M5 section 10, third trigger: no qualifying swing within 10 sessions) - a different and still-valid ground, unaffected by the corroboration correction, which removes a wrong reason to suppress but does not lower the swing-magnitude bar. The fib anchor rule starts at a 4-session lookback and extends one session at a time to a maximum of 10, seeking a swing of magnitude >= 2 x ATR14 = 2 x 63.03 = 126.06 pts. The 10-session window ends at D-1 and therefore spans 21 May - 3 June 2026 (21, 22, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29 May, 1, 2, 3 June). Recomputed on that window from the series named above, the active swing runs from the latest local low to the more recent local high: 7504.30 (27 May 2026 - a true local low, with 26 May 7505.5 and 28 May 7515.5 both higher) up to 7624.60 (2 June 2026 - a true local high, with 1 June 7623.6 and 3 June 7608.0 both lower). Magnitude 120.30 pts = 1.91x ATR14, short of the 126.06 pt bar by 5.76 pts. No other pair of local swing points inside the window qualifies: the shallower swing 7515.50 (28 May) -> 7624.60 (2 June) is 109.10 pts = 1.73x ATR14 and fails by more; the next local low back is 7339.10 (19 May), the twelfth session of the block and outside the 10-session cap. The 25-session swing 7132.70 (30 Apr) -> 7624.60 (2 June) is 491.90 pts = 7.80x ATR14 and qualifies on magnitude, but its low is the twenty-fifth session of the block; the lookback cap is the binding rule - the fib anchor may not be taken beyond 10 sessions - so the 25-day swing is rejected and the cap wins. Window-edge extremes were also rejected: the 21 May low 7394.10 measured to 7624.60 would give 230.50 pts = 3.66x ATR14, but 21 May is not a swing point at all (20 May printed a lower low of 7362.30 and 19 May a lower one still at 7339.10) - it is an artefact of where the window happens to start, and the rule reads swing points, not block extremes. The finding does not depend on the bar basis: recomputed on full broker-day bars from the same series, the latest local low inside the window is 7495.70 (28 May, with 27 May 7504.3 and 29 May 7563.1 both higher) and the swing to the 2 June high 7624.60 is 128.90 pts against the full-day ATR14 of 73.75, i.e. 1.75x - short of 2x on its own basis as well.
